question: Why must the sanctum not be split when its inner chamber is extended?
premises: The sanctum is considered in relation to splitting.
The condition involves an extended inner chamber.
inference: Splitting the sanctum when its inner chamber is extended is fault-giving and must be avoided.
uncertainties: The exact architectural action denoted by phālanīyaṃ in this context is not fully specified.
plain_english: The sanctum must not be split, for that gives fault when the inner chamber is extended.
